why: Preregistered refutation fired: the first challenger's win share rose above one half on both suites (holdout 49/96 = 51%, screen 52/96 = 54%, from a 37.5% baseline). The headline prediction also missed on holdout (cancellations fell 25.5%, target at least 30%) and acclamations reached only 0.14-0.18 (target 0.25). The prestige farmer weakened further (16.7% to 11.5% holdout wins) and the gate spread widened (west 37.5%, east 13.5%). Weakening the boost converts canceled claims into first-proclaim coronations: a worse trade for a family game than the churn it removes.
kept_numbers: Median rounds 25->23 holdout, 24->23 screen; draws unchanged; contest offered rate and affordability unchanged (0.69/0.80); all four profiles still won. Boosted-contest win rate fell 0.77 -> 0.65 as predicted; bots still bought the boost on 82% of boost-affordable turns (policy limitation, not a human choice signal).
